stem: A crop photograph is strongly color-shifted by the room lighting, and color is part of the observation being documented. What is the strongest evidence action when conditions allow?
choices: Keep the original image, document the lighting issue, and rely on the written color description instead of taking another image
Retake the image under more consistent or neutral lighting while preserving the same crop identity and observation context
Adjust white balance and saturation until the image matches the technician's memory of the plant's color
Take a sharper close-up under the same colored fixture because image sharpness matters more than color fidelity
rationale: When color is part of the evidence, a new image captured under more consistent lighting is stronger than relying on a known color-shifted image or editing the image to match memory. Identity and context still need to remain linked to the retake.
